title.narrative: Promoting Inclusive, Youth-Driven and Indigenous-Led Approaches to Combat Discrimination in Pacific SIDS

description.narrative: This work plan aims to strengthen the capacity of Pacific Member States and stakeholders to combat discrimination and racism, while promoting intercultural understanding, gender-based resilience, and disability inclusion, with a strong focus on youth, Indigenous communities, and persons with disabilities. Pacific SIDS are characterized by rich cultural diversity and strong Indigenous traditions, yet they face persistent social inequalities, exclusion, and emerging risks linked to misinformation, climate pressures, and socio-economic change. Building on UNESCO’s normative frameworks and global initiatives, the work plan will support Member States in promoting inclusive, rights-based approaches that address discrimination in all its forms. It will also foster greater understanding of shared histories and cultural identities while empowering youth and Indigenous communities to actively participate in shaping inclusive societies. Special attention will be given to disability inclusion, ensuring accessibility and equal participation across all interventions. The rationale is to address gaps in inclusive policymaking, limited awareness of discrimination issues, and insufficient engagement of marginalized groups in decision-making processes. Without targeted efforts, inequalities risk deepening, undermining social cohesion and resilience. By strengthening knowledge, fostering dialogue, and empowering key stakeholders, UNESCO will support Pacific Member States in building inclusive, equitable, and cohesive societies aligned with sustainable development priorities.
